items.subtype_name: Name the mismatch or unintended effect
items.stimulus: To help a depleted grouper population recover, regulators closed one section of a Caribbean reef to all fishing. Within three years, grouper counts inside the closed section had nearly doubled. The fishing boats that once worked that section did not leave the area, however; they moved to the reef's open edges, which they now fish far more heavily than before. Thus, an unintended effect of the closure has been ______
items.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: a decline in the grouper population inside the closed section.
an increase in the total number of boats fishing the region.
greater fishing pressure on the parts of the reef left open.
a shift among local crews toward species other than grouper.
items.explanation: The closure's goal was to protect fish, and it worked inside the closed section. The passage then says the same boats moved to the open edges and now fish them more heavily. The unintended effect is the extra pressure on the reef that is still open.

B.why: The passage says the existing boats moved. It never says more boats arrived, so you added a step the text doesn't support.

how often a bridge's visible parts are checked and how often its cable wires are.
the strength of the steel cable wires and the strength of the bridge's towers.
how quickly the cable wires corrode and how quickly the deck's steel corrodes.

items.subtype_name: Name the mismatch or unintended effect
items.stimulus: Many people assume that how well a vaccine protects depends only on the vaccine itself. Immunologists point out, however, that the response a vaccine triggers can vary with the recipient's age. items.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: leaving younger recipients less protected than older recipients.
making the vaccine less effective for recipients of every age.
raising the cost of producing and distributing the vaccine.
leaving older recipients less protected than younger recipients.
items.explanation: The passage says older adults produce fewer antibodies from the same dose. So when everyone gets one standard dose, older recipients end up less protected than younger ones.

A.why: You reversed the two groups. The passage says older adults, not younger ones, respond more weakly to the same dose.

B.why: This is strength creep. The passage describes a weaker response in one age group only, not across every age.

lower toll revenue than city officials had originally projected.

items.subtype_name: Name the mismatch or unintended effect
items.stimulus: In 2019 a regional government required employers to offer health insurance to any employee working at least 30 hours a week. The goal was to extend coverage to part-time workers, who often had none. Some labour economists warned, however, that employers could avoid the new cost by keeping schedules at 29 hours or fewer. If that happened, the rule would have the unintended effect of ______
items.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: raising insurance costs for employees who already worked full-time schedules.
reducing the hours available to the part-time workers it was meant to help.
encouraging employers to move most part-time staff into full-time positions.
removing health coverage from every part-time worker in the entire region.
items.explanation: The rule was meant to protect part-time workers. The economists' warning is that employers would cap shifts at 29 hours. That cap falls on part-time workers, so the rule would cut hours for the very group it was written to help. An unintended effect usually works against the policy's own goal, and this one does.

A.why: You picked a cost to full-time workers, but the passage never mentions them. The tension is between the rule's goal and its effect on part-time workers, not on a group it never targeted.

C.why: You reversed the warning. The economists expected employers to cut schedules to below 30 hours, not raise workers to full-time positions.

D.why: You jumped from 'could keep schedules short' to 'every part-time worker loses coverage.' Most of these workers had no coverage to lose, and 'every' goes far beyond a warning that something could happen.

how large high-latitude regions look and how much area they actually cover.

the size of Greenland on the map and the number of people who live there.

running more slowly in the race the routine was meant to prepare for.
suffering more muscle injuries than runners who never stretch at all.

items.subtype_name: Name the mismatch or unintended effect

items.stimulus: Graphene is often described as the simplest of materials: a single flat sheet of carbon atoms. Making it is anything but simple. Large sheets free of defects require extreme heat, spotless surfaces, and a delicate transfer step in which the sheet can easily tear.
items.stem: Which choice names the two things the passage sets against each other?

how simple graphene's structure is and how hard it is to make
how thin graphene's sheets are and how much heat they can withstand
items.explanation: The passage opens with what seems simple, graphene's structure as a single sheet of atoms. Then it turns with 'anything but simple' to what is demanding: producing the material. items.stimulus: To protect young patients from infection, a hospital began screening every visitor to its children's ward for fever. items.subtype_name: Name the mismatch or unintended effect

shift the floods it prevents upstream onto communities located farther downstream.
protect the new homes and businesses behind it from most of the river's floods.
increase the amount of property exposed to floods larger than it can withstand.

items.stimulus: A city offered free flu vaccinations at clinics open only on weekday mornings, aiming to narrow the gap in vaccination rates between its low-income residents and everyone else. led hourly workers to distrust health programs that are run by the city.
lowered vaccination rates among low-income residents below their earlier level.

items.subtype_name: Name the mismatch or unintended effect
items.stimulus: To treat patients with active infections, some blood centers give them antibody-rich plasma from recovered donors. Only plasma that clears a high antibody threshold, however, is labeled "high-titer" and released for this use. The threshold is meant to ensure that recipients get the most protective plasma. prevent recovered donors from giving plasma for any purpose at all.
reduce the supply of plasma available to the patients it was designed to protect.
cause donors' antibody levels to fall before they are permitted to donate.
items.explanation: The two sides of the tension are a goal (give patients the most protective plasma) and a timing gap (most donors give blood only after their antibody levels have already started to drop).
